notes.title: Resolution increases and graphical updates
notes.notes:
The original version of The Spirit Engine was created in an era of bulky 4:3 cathode ray tube monitors, where 640x480 was the most common screen resolution. The game ran in a 490x400 window and that seemed OK at the time.

Twenty years later, desktop displays look very different! TSEDX supports a range of resolutions up to 3840x1080 (32:9) and 3840x2160 (4K)!. This is over ten times the visible area to display. Since the original game is scrolling, the task didn’t seem too daunting - until we got to work.

First, the entire UI needed to be re-designed. Most of the backgrounds needed to be drawn outwards to support larger screens, from deserts and marshes to trains and skyscrapers. Some skill effects relied upon a fixed top screen edge. Even one notable boss whose body used to be off-screen now needed to be drawn in its entirety. Some of the cutscenes rely on characters appearing from off-screen positions and so we’ve needed to come up with clever new ways to rewrite their entrances.

Below are two example cutscenes that needed a lot of work to scale up from their original 490x400px display, both involving methods of transport (click for the full versions):

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45396282/ffdc7f5ece58e8a61eee9d08e36b60ae4936b9bd.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45396282/ffdc7f5ece58e8a61eee9d08e36b60ae4936b9bd.png[/img][/url]

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45396282/98197ad9517a465da733691225509a2edc8b33b0.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45396282/98197ad9517a465da733691225509a2edc8b33b0.png[/img][/url]

We chose 1920px and 600px as our upper limits for width and height respectively. 1920px width was needed to support 32:9 if we wanted to keep a 540px height that could scale, and 600px is intended for 16:10 resolutions.

Going past a 960px width for a pixel game is rarely explored due to the work required, but we think the effort has been worth it!

- Mark and Aquellex

notes.title: The History of The Spirit Engine
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45396282/ba3e6ba4e18aeef6b887c9b5e9cb421f27e083bb.png[/img]

“Can a real-time, side-scrolling action RPG be fun?”

This was the question I asked back in 2001. I was at university and playing Seiken Densetsu 3, a classic top-down 2D action RPG on the SNES. I wanted to make something similar, but with a twist. It would be side-on like the platformers that remain popular with indie developers and it would be real-time, without the need to pause and navigate menus during combat. And I knew how to make it.

In the early 1990s the revolutionary game development software ‘Klik & Play’ was released for Windows 3.11. It let amateur developers create games without needing to learn a traditional programming language and while new versions of the software have followed, the concept has remained the same.
A thriving amateur development community soon grew up around ‘Klik’ products. I sold my SNES to get the money to buy a copy of ‘Klik & Play’ and get involved. Websites and IRC channels formed, followed by small indie studios, one of which was Natomic, led by Andi Smith.

It was as a member of Natomic and with the playtesting help of fellow members that ‘The Spirit Engine’ was developed over the two years I spent at university. Early iterations of the game included platforms and jumping but these were eventually removed, resulting in the game’s signature 2D side-on view and real-time battle engine.

The final game was released in 2003. It was experimental and rough around the edges but it found fans and eventually spawned a sequel. Sadly there have been no obvious successors in the twenty years since and this is disappointing if you wanted to play more!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45396282/54c35e5234884ea468d6f89614b2fac19516871e.png[/img]

Being unpolished made TSE1 a great candidate to revisit when Aquellex started work on an update several years ago. And TSEDX is not just a remaster, but a complete rebuild of the original game for modern systems, with a new engine, new features, updated graphics and revised dialogue. The upgrade is so comprehensive that it’s impossible to go back to the original release. We’re excited about what DX has become and we hope that you will be too when it’s released later this year.

- Mark

notes.title: Roadmap
notes.notes:
As of this post, the game's campaign has been fully ported over, and the rest of our time will be used for extensive polish. Our priorities include:

[olist]
[*] Overhauling the game menus and UI 
[*] Revamping all the art to support modern widescreen resolutions
[*] Redesigning the two 1v1 fights from the original game into more exciting and dynamic 3v3 fights.
[*] Adding context-sensitive defeat tips to the game-over screen
[*] Adding Steam achievements
[*] Supporting many more save slots  
[*] Preparing a playable demo
[*] And of course many more quality-of-life improvements!
[/olist]

TSEDX has an active Discord as well. Come find us in [url=https://discord.gg/tQGvmM2]the Discord[/url], and if you played the original game you may even find some old friends there!

Best wishes,
~aqx
